name: When should I consider replacing a floor transition instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing a floor transition instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing a floor transition if the damage is extensive, such as severe splintering, major breaks, or significant water damage that has compromised the integrity of the material or subfloor. If the transition strip is severely warped, discolored beyond repair, or if continuous repairs are needed, replacement offers a more lasting solution. Additionally, if you're updating your flooring or desire a different aesthetic, replacing the transition can improve the overall look and performance of your space. Our experts can help you make this decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace a transition if damage is severe, like extensive breaks, water damage, or if it's repeatedly failing after repairs.
